description.narrative: 1 Organisations levelThe applicant in the open call for cycles needs to apply with a partnership of a minimum of 2 other CSOs from their own city/region, therefore a minimum of 3 CSOs are cocreating and coapplying alongside each other. By implementing this structure, we force applicants to work closely together, think about distributing tasks and responsibilities among one another, and therefore reinforce collaboration on a local and/or regional level. In doing so, there is already a bestpracticeexchange component taking place, as different organizations will prove to have different experiences and expertise for executing different tasks within the consortium. This collaboration contributes to a strengthened ecosystem of CSOs in Albania, where intrasectoral cooperation instances are scarce. For example, cycle 1(Tirana) winners, Social Contract Institute, PIF and DoArt, had never worked together before. In their reporting, however, SCI mentioned that they will work together for the future thanks to this experience in the Artivist Stafete project.2 Financial and institutional capacitiesThe project contributes not only to increased capacities in terms of collaborations and project management, it also contributes to the financial and institutional capacity of coapplicants and subgrantees. Both Act for Society and OMSA grew through the hiring of financial staff (Pajtim Shehu for Act for Society) and experts in the field of subgranting(Sonila Necaj for OMSA). Both Pajtim and Sonila are guiding and mentoring subgrantees in the financial aspects of the project agreements. For example, staff members of our creative bub TEK BUNKERI utilized the extra financial support offered by Act for Society in structuring their administration and financial systems. Some of the granted CSOs (outside Tirana needed extra support and guidance on their reporting capacities on activitiesand providing a comprehensive narrative and financial reports.Also, both organisations hire staff members to get skilled in artivism methodologies. This will contribute to the sustainability of project goals in the long run as well.3 Fostering better collaboration of Albanian CSOs Pivotal to achieving Oct2 is the interconnection of local CSOs through online and offline project activities and platforms, such as training, public presentations and online work spaces. Through the `cycle concept. grantees attend each others hackathons and launches, therefore transferring the gained knowledge and experiences from one city to another in anorganised and periodical scheme. The public presentations of both CSO, as well as youngsters, activists and changemakers, are key to the dissemination of project results, furthermore energising target audiences in other cities and localities. The grand notionbehind the cycle concept is the format of the `Stafete: the exchange of knowledge and peertopeer learning of CSOs.All activities within the action are therefore geared towards strengthening the CSO sector.For example, the hackathons function both as the concluding event of a cycle, as well as the instance where the CSO in charge of the next cycle is relayed and `hands over the `ArtivistStafet torch. The next cycles launch event will be attended by participating CSOs of the previous cycle, using the instance as a bestpractices exchange opportunity. Activities toconnect the aforementioned ecosystem will be the centre of focus for the next year, activities especially in the online hub activities, but also the community gatherings in Tek Bunkeri, the introduction of quarterly RoundTables with CSOs and `alumni networking events for all subgrantees.
